nh_thin_air.notes: Start straight up (5.5) or from the easier left side (5.3) to a ledge, then climb a flake system with angular blocks to the anchor, roughly 50 ft.

A long rightward traverse along a natural weakness, clipping three fixed pins. One slightly tricky 5.6 move is the mental crux for many; protect the second carefully. About 70 ft; can be linked with pitch 1.
Up slabs to a flake leading into a short chimney, exiting onto a ledge. About 70 ft.

The longest and best pitch, about 130 ft: follow the crack system to a small overhang, then layback up a flake (the 5.6 crux) to tree anchors. A short scramble over roots and dirt reaches the large ledge used for the walk-off.

nv_dark_shadows.notes: Easy start with two good bolts to the anchor. Pitches 1 and 2 can be climbed as one 170 ft pitch, so a 60 m rope is helpful.
From the bolt anchor, take the right-facing desert-varnished dihedral for about 60 ft, then move left to the belay anchors.
Keep following the fine crack, stemming where it helps, for about 120 ft to the next bolted station. Expect the varnished rock to feel slick.
Leave the anchor rightward onto the arching crack and take it to the last bolted station, tucked under the huge roof. On the descent, watch that the ropes do not wedge in this same crack.

wa_boving_christensen.notes: Begin toward the west end of the south face, roughly 100 ft right of Solid Gold. A short crack leads to a low-angle slab below a corner; follow the corner to a belay under a steep white face. The route sees little traffic, so test the rock, which can be loose in places.

A long pitch up exposed, somewhat dirty face cracks that are lined with lichen, trending a bit leftward to a ledge below a sharp corner. The line wanders, so expect heavy rope drag by the top; extend runners generously. Climb carefully on the lichen.
The best pitch on the route. A fun bouldery move gets you into the clean corner, which you follow before exiting right into an alcove for the belay.

Starts with a finger crack on a slab (around 5.10b) that widens to hands before a step left into a flake. The crack can thin back to fingers above the hand section, so carry small cams and place them before the thin part. Finish up the last hand cracks (about 5.8) to the West Ridge, where several nearby south-face routes top out. The first-ascent party climbed this with nuts and hexes only.

wa_bowling_alley_aka_regular_route.notes: 40m through the gully to a saddle; 4–5 bolts, slings to a chain anchor.
Vertical groove past large rock formations, traversing to join the Regular Route line; 11 bolts to chains.
Grooved ledge and a knobby ramp to 3 bolts and chain anchors.
Climbs through a band of basalt to a chimney, then leftward up a low-angle chute to the summit; 5 clips.
